writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues beetles, bears, and frost-damaged roots explain the cedar decline; lecture rebuts each: beetles only attack already-sick trees, bears are absent where decline still occurs, and more trees die at warmer low elevations, contradicting frost damage.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture doubts that the bone-channel material, iron-filled spheres, and collagen come from dinosaur tissue, offering bacterial residue, mineral origins, and modern contamination as alternatives.
writingIntegrated.k: 공룡 뼈 속 부드러운 물질, 붉은 구체, 콜라겐이 원래 조직이라는 주장을 세 가지 근거로 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues that soft tissue, blood-cell-like spheres, and collagen in a T. rex bone are original dinosaur remains; the lecture rebuts each point: the material is bacterial residue, the spheres also appear in animals without blood cells so they are mineral, and the collagen is likely from recent human contamination.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture argues that the ancient jars could well have been batteries, challenging the reading's three objections point by point.
writingIntegrated.k: 강의는 고대 항아리가 전지였을 가능성을 주장하며, 읽기 지문의 세 가지 반론을 하나씩 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues the vessels were not ancient batteries; the lecture rebuts each of its three points: the missing wires were likely overlooked by untrained finders, the copper cylinders may have been repurposed from scroll storage, and the shocks and healing uses could explain the battery's role.

writingIntegrated.g: Zebra mussels can be controlled by changing ballast water practices, birds may prey on them, and fish populations may not decline overall.
writingIntegrated.k: 얼룩무늬 홍합의 확산은 통제할 수 있고, 어족에 대한 위협도 과장되었다는 주장
writingIntegrated.c: The reading claims zebra mussels can be controlled and are not a serious fish threat; the lecture rebuts by saying ballast water exchange at sea kills them, birds adapt to eat them, and bottom-feeding fish may benefit from the nutrients they produce.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture argues that the reading's three explanations for the Little Ice Age fail: the Gulf Stream idea ignores southern cooling, volcanic dust would have left visible traces, and forest regrowth was too brief to matter.
writingIntegrated.k: 강의는 읽기 지문의 세 가설(걸프 해류, 화산, 농지 숲 복원)이 소빙하기를 설명하지 못한다고 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues three causes (Gulf Stream disruption, volcanic eruptions, reforestation of farmland) explain the Little Ice Age; the lecture rebuts each: Gulf Stream cannot explain Southern Hemisphere cooling, no reports of dust-related sky effects, and forests did not last long enough.

writingIntegrated.g: Evidence supporting Peary's claim to the North Pole is unreliable: the committee was biased, his speed is incomparable to a later trip, and his photos cannot establish position.
writingIntegrated.k: 피어리의 북극 도달 주장을 뒷받침하는 증거들은 신뢰하기 어렵다는 반박 논리
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues Peary's North Pole claim is unproven; the lecture rebuts each reading point—committee was biased, Avery's trip differed in conditions and supplies, and the faded photos cannot reliably fix the Sun's position.

writingIntegrated.g: The reading rejects the idea that Edmontosaurs migrated each winter, arguing they could find food locally, that herding does not imply migration, and that juveniles could not have travelled far.
writingIntegrated.k: 에드몬토사우루스가 겨울마다 이동했다는 가설은 설득력이 없으며, 먹이 확보, 무리 생활의 이유, 어린 개체의 이동 능력이라는 세 가지 근거로 이를 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues the Edmontosaurs stayed in the North Slope year-round (summer plant growth left dead vegetation for winter food, herd living has other purposes, juveniles could not migrate); the lecture's rebuttal is not included in this excerpt.

writingIntegrated.g: The claim that an ancient burning mirror was impractical and technically impossible is not convincing.
writingIntegrated.k: 고대 연소 거울이 비실용적이거나 기술적으로 불가능했다는 주장은 설득력이 없다는 반박
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: the burning mirror was impractical and impossible to build or use; Lecture rebuts with three points: mirror pieces could form a parabola, pitch on the ships would ignite quickly, and a hidden mirror fire would be more effective than flaming arrows.

writingIntegrated.g: The fossil lines on the dinosaur are most likely true feathers rather than decay artifacts or frills, and three critic arguments against this are weak.
writingIntegrated.k: 공룡 화석의 선 모양 구조는 부패 흔적이 아니라 깃털이며, 이를 반박하는 세 가지 주장은 설득력이 없다는 내용
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues the fossil lines are feathers and rebuts three critic claims: decay, frills (no beta-keratin), and non-flight function (display, supported by color analysis).

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture rebuts three proposed uses of the carved Neolithic stone balls: as hunting or fighting weapons, as weights, and as status markers.
writingIntegrated.k: 강의는 신석기 석구가 무기, 저울추, 사회적 지위의 상징이었다는 세 가지 이론을 각각 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues the balls served as weapons, weighing tools, or social markers; the lecture counters that they show no weapon wear, their masses vary with stone density, and they are absent from graves.

writingIntegrated.g: Each of the three proposed explanations for the sea cow's extinction has flaws, suggesting a longer-running cause that predates European arrival.
writingIntegrated.k: 스텔러바다소 멸종의 원인으로 제시된 세 가지 이론은 각각 뒷받침하기 어렵고, 원인은 유럽인 도착 이전부터 진행된 다른 요인일 가능성이 크다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: native Siberian hunting, a kelp decline from ecological disturbance, and European traders each caused extinction; Lecture: each is rebutted: hunting was too limited to matter, no wider ecosystem decline was observed, and the population was already shrinking before Europeans arrived.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture argues that none of the three proposed authors likely wrote the Voynich manuscript, countering each reading claim with evidence.
writingIntegrated.k: 강의는 읽기 지문이 든 세 후보 중 누구도 보이니치 필사본의 작성자가 아니라는 주장을 세 가지 근거로 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: the three named people are plausible authors of the manuscript. Lecture: each candidate is ruled out, Ascham by his ordinary work, Kelley by the unnecessary effort the code would take for a fake, and Voynich by the radiocarbon-style dating showing the materials predate him.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture casts doubt on cloud seeding's success by challenging the reading's three supporting points: lab results don't transfer to real clouds, Asian urban results may not apply to US farmland, and the regional hail decline may be natural weather variation.
writingIntegrated.k: 구름 씨뿌리기의 효과를 의심할 만한 세 가지 근거를 반박하는 강의 내용
writingIntegrated.c: Reading claims cloud seeding reduces hail damage; lecture rebuts with three points: silver iodide can suppress precipitation (causing drought), urban pollution-driven results don't transfer to unpolluted US farms, and the local hail drop across neighboring areas suggests natural weather variation.

writingIntegrated.s: turtle excluder devices in shrimp fishing
writingIntegrated.g: Turtle excluder devices should be standard on shrimp boats because the combined catch of many boats threatens endangered turtles, enforcing TED rules is easier than enforcing time limits, and any size problem can be fixed by redesigning the devices.
writingIntegrated.k: 거북이 배제 장치(TED)는 새우잡이 배에서 바다거북을 보호하는 데 효과적이며 필수 장비가 되어야 한다는 주장에 대한 반박
writingIntegrated.c: The reading criticizes TEDs as impractical; the lecture rebuts each criticism in turn: the impact is cumulative across the whole fleet, TED rules are easier to enforce than time limits, and the size problem can be solved by modifying the design.

writingIntegrated.g: A station floating about 50 km above Venus could avoid crushing pressure, make its own water and oxygen from atmospheric compounds, and generate ample power from filtered and reflected sunlight.
writingIntegrated.k: 금성 대기 위에 떠 있는 기지는 기압, 물·산소 확보, 전력 문제를 해결할 수 있어 실현 가능하다는 주장
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues a permanent Venus station is too difficult; lecture rebuts each of the three problems (pressure, water/oxygen, light/power) by proposing a floating station at about 50 km altitude.

writingIntegrated.g: Stricter coal ash rules are needed, covering old disposal sites too, since mercury's safe recycling history suggests consumers won't shy away, and the added cost is small.
writingIntegrated.k: 석탄재 처리와 폐기에 대한 규제를 강화해야 한다는 주장
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: stricter coal ash rules are needed (liners for old sites, recycling safety, affordable cost). Lecture rebuttal is not included in this excerpt.

writingIntegrated.g: The three proposed remedies for birds striking buildings would each fail, since birds misread mirrors, open gaps, and magnetic cues in different ways.
writingIntegrated.k: 새가 유리창에 부딪히는 문제를 막는 세 가지 방안은 각각 실효성이 낮다고 주장한다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: three proposed fixes (one-way glass, striped patterns, artificial magnetic fields) would not work; Lecture: rebuts each point, arguing one-way glass reflects like a mirror, open spaces look like holes, and birds use magnetism only over long distances, not for short city flights.

writingIntegrated.g: Each of three proposed lifestyles for agnostids (predator, seafloor dweller, parasite) is undermined by fossil evidence about their eyes, mobility, and population size.
writingIntegrated.k: 고대 절지동물 agnostid의 생활 방식에 대한 세 가지 가설이 각각 약점을 가지고 있다는 내용
writingIntegrated.c: Reading claims three theories (predator, seafloor dweller, parasite) are flawed; lecture rebuts each by showing the reasons given for rejecting them are not valid or are contradicted by other evidence.

writingIntegrated.s: Norse silver coin found in Maine
writingIntegrated.g: Many archaeologists argue the Maine coin is authentic evidence of contact between Norse explorers and Native Americans, and that objections to it have simple explanations.
writingIntegrated.k: 메인주에서 발견된 노르드 은화는 위조가 아니라 천 년 전 노르드인과 원주민의 접촉을 보여주는 진짜 증거라는 주장이다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues the coin is a fake; lecture rebuts with three points: other distant objects at the site came via Native American trade travel, Norse likely took their coins home when they left, and Native Americans may have valued the coins as attractive jewelry rather than money.

writingIntegrated.g: Bees may well have built the nests found in 200-million-year-old fossilized trees, and the skeptics' three objections do not hold up.
writingIntegrated.k: 2억 년 전 화석 나무 속 둥지를 벌이 만들었을 가능성은 충분하며, 이에 대한 회의론자들의 세 가지 반론은 설득력이 없다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: the ancient nests may not be bee-made because no fossil bees from that era exist, bees likely postdate flowering plants, and the chambers lack spiral caps. Lecture rebuttal: bees were rarely preserved then because the resin-producing trees were scarce, bees could have fed on non-flowering plants before flowers evolved, and the chambers' waterproofing chemistry matches modern bees.

writingIntegrated.g: New evidence suggests pterosaurs could have flown under their own power, countering three earlier objections.
writingIntegrated.k: 최근 연구는 익룡이 동력 비행을 할 수 있었을 가능성을 보여준다고 주장한다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues pterosaurs could fly via powered flight (warm-blooded metabolism, light hollow bones, four-limb takeoff); the lecture rebuts each point by arguing the reading's evidence is inadequate or that the supporting claims don't hold.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture argues that all three proposed remedies for declining frog numbers fail: pesticide limits are unfair to farmers, fungus treatments are too costly to apply at scale, and habitat protection ignores that global warming is the real threat.
writingIntegrated.k: 개구리 개체수 감소를 막으려는 세 가지 제안은 각각 비현실적이거나 비용이 많이 들거나 효과가 없다는 강의 내용
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: the three methods (cutting pesticides, treating the skin fungus, protecting water and wetlands) would save frogs. Lecture: each is impractical, since pesticide limits hurt farmers economically, fungus treatments must be repeated for every generation, and habitat protection cannot stop warming-driven habitat loss.

writingIntegrated.g: Each of three obstacles to a Mars crew (food, water, and air; zero gravity; solar radiation) has a workable solution, so the mission is feasible.
writingIntegrated.k: 화성 유인 탐사의 세 가지 문제(식량·물·산소, 무중력, 태양 복사)에 대해 수경재배, 운동·영양 관리, 차폐 대피 등으로 해결 가능하다는 설명
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues that the three problems make a Mars trip unfeasible; the lecture rebuts each point with a specific solution (hydroponics, exercise and supplements, monitored shelters).

writingIntegrated.g: Three popular beliefs about elephants are explained by simpler causes: aging elephants wander for food, painting is trained rather than artistic, and fear of mice stems from unfamiliarity.
writingIntegrated.k: 코끼리에 관한 세 가지 통념(노령 코끼리의 죽음 인지, 그림 능력, 쥐에 대한 공포)은 실제로는 다른 원인으로 설명된다고 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading claims elephants show awareness of death, artistic skill, and fear of mice; the lecture rebuts each point: old elephants leave herds to find softer food near water, painting results from ear-touch training without understanding, and mouse fear reflects unfamiliarity that fades with exposure.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture argues that asteroid colonization is impractical because low gravity harms health, mining profits are uncertain, and unusual orbits make return difficult.
writingIntegrated.k: 소행성 식민지 건설은 중력, 채광 수익, 귀환 문제 때문에 실현 가능성이 낮다는 강의의 반박
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues that asteroid colonization is feasible on three points (easy landing, valuable metals, easy access), and the lecture rebuts each: low gravity causes health problems, metal profits are reduced by costs and falling prices, and unusual orbits make the asteroid hard to return from.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture challenges three claimed benefits of taxing cigarettes and unhealthy goods: the taxes may not change behavior for the better, they burden low-income people unfairly, and governments may become financially dependent on the revenue.
writingIntegrated.k: 담배와 건강에 해로운 식품에 매기는 세금의 세 가지 장점을 하나씩 반박하는 강의
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: such taxes improve health, are fair, and fund useful projects. Lecture: they may push smokers toward cheaper, more harmful products, are unfair to lower earners, and give governments an incentive not to pursue stronger anti-smoking measures.

writingIntegrated.g: The three proposed fixes for the lake's rising salt—desalination, importing seawater, and walling off sections—each fail in practice due to health hazards, prohibitive cost, and earthquake damage.
writingIntegrated.k: 염도 문제의 세 가지 해결책(담수화, 해수 유입, 벽으로 구획)은 각각 건강 위험, 높은 건설 비용, 지진에 따른 붕괴 때문에 현실성이 낮다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues the three remedies for the lake's salinity are workable; the lecture rebuts each: desalination leaves toxic residue that could be windborne, seawater import needs costly pipelines or canals over 100 km, and walls would collapse in earthquakes and let salty water mix back in.

writingIntegrated.g: Objections to using box-shaped devices to grow trees against desertification are weak: the devices are reusable and affordable, local residents gain tangible benefits, and the trees survive after the devices are removed.
writingIntegrated.k: 사막화를 막기 위해 상자 모양 장치로 나무를 키우는 방식에 대한 반대 의견은 설득력이 부족하며, 비용·관리·생존력 측면에서 각각 반박된다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading opposes the devices on cost, local burden, and weak survival; the lecture rebuts each point by showing the devices are reusable, locals gain food and firewood, and roots let trees thrive after removal.

writingIntegrated.g: Three proposed explanations for the 52 hertz whale's unusual song each fail when examined, so the whale's uniqueness remains unexplained.
writingIntegrated.k: 52헤르츠 고래의 특이한 노래를 설명하려는 세 가지 가설은 모두 결함이 있어 이 고래의 독특함은 여전히 수수께끼로 남는다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading-side theories (hybrid origin, hearing loss, membership in a rare species) are proposed; the lecture rebuts each: the whale migrates alone unlike known hybrids, throat structure is unrelated to hearing, and decades of underwater recordings show no earlier similar songs or parents.

writingIntegrated.g: The government should keep Amtrak public, arguing that it serves remote areas, that other transport modes also receive state support, and that better funding would make trains more popular.
writingIntegrated.k: 정부가 Amtrak을 민간에 팔아서는 안 되며, 노선 보전, 항공 등 다른 교통수단에 대한 정부 지원, 철도 투자 필요성을 근거로 든다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: argues against selling Amtrak to a private firm, using three points (remote-route service, government support for competitors, and the need for investment). Lecture rebuttal is not included in this excerpt.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture contends that popular accounts of Spartacus are historically unreliable, so the reading's claims built on them don't hold up.
writingIntegrated.k: 강의는 스파르타쿠스에 관한 널리 알려진 이야기들이 역사적 근거가 부족하며, 독서 지문이 이 부정확한 이야기에 의존하고 있다고 지적한다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading presents Spartacus as a noble freedom fighter seeking home and liberation for all slaves; lecture rebuts each point: his goals were revenge and wealth, his battle wins came from weak Roman units not genius, and the liberation story was an 18th-century anti-slavery play rather than history.

writingIntegrated.g: The lecture rejects three proposed uses for the Plain of Jars (fermentation, water storage for travelers, and burial tombs) and concludes its purpose remains unknown.
writingIntegrated.k: 라오스 항아리 평원의 용도로 제시된 발효, 식수 저장, 무덤이라는 세 가설을 강의가 각각 반박한다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading argues the jars served fermentation, water storage, or burial; the lecture rebuts each: clay pots were easier for fermentation, travelers near rivers needed no stored water, and uncovered jars would not protect remains.

writingIntegrated.g: Three proposed remedies for rhino poaching (removing horns, educating consumers, legalizing horn sales) would each fail or backfire.
writingIntegrated.k: 코뿔소 뿔 밀렵을 막기 위한 세 가지 해결책(뿔 제거, 소비자 교육, 합법적 판매)은 각각 실효성이 낮거나 오히려 역효과가 날 수 있다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading proposes de-horning, consumer education, and legal horn sales to save rhinos; the lecture rebuts all three as impractical, ineffective, or likely to increase poaching.

writingIntegrated.g: The reading argues that three proposed remedies for the golden frog decline would each fail: the protective bacterium wears off quickly, released captive-bred frogs would be reinfected by carriers in the wild, and the heat-based defense drains energy and weakens the frogs.
writingIntegrated.k: 황금개구리 개체군 회복을 위해 제시된 세 가지 방안이 모두 효과가 없을 것이라는 주장
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: all three proposed solutions (protective bacterium, captive-bred releases, heat-based self-defense) will fail for specific reasons; the lecture's rebuttal of these points is not included in this excerpt.

writingIntegrated.g: Artificial reefs may do more harm than good: higher catches don't prove fish populations grew, secret reef locations create safety hazards, and reefs can damage the seafloor when they break apart.
writingIntegrated.k: 인공 어초는 물고기 수 증가 착시, 안전 문제, 환경 피해를 일으켜 이익보다 문제가 크다는 주장
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: artificial reefs cause more problems than benefits, supported by three points (misleading catch data, safety risks of secret reefs, environmental damage from loose reef material); lecture rebuttal not included in this excerpt.

writingIntegrated.g: Three proposed methods for controlling cheatgrass are unlikely to succeed: grazers eat native plants first, fire doesn't kill buried seeds, and the fungus only harms already-weak plants.
writingIntegrated.k: 뒤영(?) 대신 원문 요지: cheatgrass 방제 방법 세 가지가 효과적이지 않다는 주장
writingIntegrated.c: The reading claims grazing, burning, and introducing a fungal parasite would fail to control cheatgrass; the lecture rebuts each point, arguing grazers and fire and the fungus can in fact work as intended.

writingIntegrated.g: The reading doubts that a new east-coast broccoli variety delivers its promised benefits, citing offset costs, consumer distrust of its sponsors, and existing local greens like kale.
writingIntegrated.k: 동해안 브로콜리 신품종의 장점이 과장되었다는 주장: 비용 절감 효과 상쇄, 기업에 대한 소비자 불신, 케일 등 대체 채소 존재를 근거로 든다.
writingIntegrated.c: The reading argues the new east-coast broccoli will not be cheaper, trusted, or uniquely healthy; the lecture is expected to rebut each point (e.g., savings and yield trade-offs, distinct trust issues, and kale's limits).

writingIntegrated.g: Researchers have found workable answers to three concerns about tuna farming: dependence on wild young, reliance on fish-based protein feed, and parasite infestations.
writingIntegrated.k: 참치 양식의 세 가지 문제(야생 치어 의존, 고단백 먹이, 기생충 감염)에 대해 연구자들이 해결책을 찾고 있다는 내용이다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading: the three tuna-farming concerns are solvable (hormone-induced egg laying, plant-based feed, moving cages to deeper water); the lecture's rebuttal is not included in this excerpt.

writingIntegrated.g: Airships may save fuel, but they face three obstacles: unsafe or costly lifting gases, difficulty staying steady when loading cargo, and fuel limits that keep them from replacing satellites.
writingIntegrated.k: 비행선은 연료 효율이 높아도 가스 안전성·비용, 화물 적재 시 안정성, 고고도 연료 소모 문제 때문에 널리 쓰이기 어렵다.
writingIntegrated.c: Reading claims airships will become widely used due to fuel efficiency; the lecture rebuts with three points: gas safety and cost, instability during cargo pickup, and inability to match satellites' continuous high-altitude service.

speakingQ2.g: Students debate a letter opposing a new campus sculpture: one dismisses its reasons as unfounded, while the other concludes the objection is really about keeping a convenient lawn spot.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 잔디밭에 새 조각상을 세우는 계획을 두고, 한 학생은 반대 의견을 타당하지 않다고 보고 다른 학생은 그 반대가 편의 때문이라고 해석한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to place a donor-funded sculpture on the lawn. Woman: supports the sculpture and rejects Paul's reasons as baseless. Man: sees the space concern as valid at first, then decides Paul is really just resisting having to move his soccer games.

speakingQ2.s: campus bus route and parking plan
speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a university plan to cut bus service and add parking; one opposes it and blames the outdated route, while the other partly agrees that the plan would worsen congestion.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 버스 노선을 줄이고 주차장을 늘리려는 계획을 두고, 한 학생은 반대하고 다른 학생은 일부 동의한다.
speakingQ2.c: campus issue: university plan to reduce bus service and expand parking; the man opposes it (outdated route, more driving, noise and traffic), while the woman initially sees the buses as wasteful and then partly concedes that more bus use would be better.

speakingQ2.g: Two students disagree about a campus dining announcement: one doubts the healthiness claim about yogurt versus hot breakfast options, the other sees the cost-cutting plan as backfiring.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들은 캠퍼스 식당의 따뜻하고 차가운 메뉴 변경과 비용 절감 방안에 대해 서로 다른 의견을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the dining announcement promoting yogurt as healthier than hot breakfast items and cutting costs. Woman: the claim is ridiculous, hot meals are healthier, and cutbacks will push students to pricier off-campus options. Man: agrees with her on the hot-versus-cold point but doesn't dispute it further.

speakingQ2.g: A student doubts that keeping campus buildings open later would help, since most students are already booked at night, and argues that adding computers is cheaper than hiring staff for extended hours.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들이 밤 시간에 바빠 야간 개방 방안은 효과가 없으며, 비용 면에서도 교사 고용 대신 컴퓨터 추가 확충이 낫다는 의견 충돌
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: extending academic building hours at night to ease computer access; Man opposes it (students busy at night, hiring teachers too costly, add computers instead); Woman partly agrees, citing her own full schedule.

speakingQ2.g: Two students weigh whether a program where culinary students cook meals for paying diners is worthwhile, given the extra pressure and cost.
speakingQ2.k: 요리 전공 학생들이 대중을 상대로 식사를 준비하는 프로그램의 실제 가치와 비용을 두고 두 학생이 의견을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a new program where culinary students cook for public diners. Man (supporter): the high-pressure cooking is valuable practice and the meals are a cheaper alternative to fancy restaurants, so it's worth it. Woman (skeptic): students already cook in class, so the program adds little, and she questions the extra cost.

speakingQ2.g: The woman opposes a proposal to shorten History seminars, arguing the final hour is when the most valuable discussion happens, and dismisses the proposer's sleepiness-based concern.
speakingQ2.k: 역사학과 세미나 시간 단축 제안을 두고, 여학생은 반대하며 마지막 시간이 가장 활발한 토론 시간이라고 주장한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether the History department should shorten seminars (Tim's proposal to cut the last hour). Woman opposes, saying the last hour is the most engaging discussion; man is sympathetic to the proposal's reasoning that a sleepy student cannot follow, but the woman says the problem lies with Tim, not the seminar format.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a university's plan to cut art department courses and reduce faculty, with the woman objecting to the cuts and proposing alternatives.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 두 명이 예술학과 선택 과목 폐지와 교수 감축 방침에 대해 서로 다른 해결책을 논의한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university is eliminating optional art courses due to low enrollment and cutting a professor. The woman opposes the cuts, arguing enrollment is low because required painting and drawing courses crowd out electives, so requirements should change; she also suggests hiring a part-time instructor or having faculty with secondary specialties teach. The man is more receptive to the professor issue and does not fully endorse her view on the cuts.

speakingQ2.g: The university plans to play classical music during lunch; the man opposes it, arguing it will distract students who study then and that most don't enjoy classical music, and the woman agrees with him.
speakingQ2.k: 학교가 점심시간에 클래식 음악을 틀겠다는 계획을 두고, 남학생은 공부 방해와 음악 취향 문제로 반대하고 여학생은 그 의견에 동의한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: university plan to play classical music at lunchtime. Man opposes (distracting for students studying, most dislike classical, students will just use mp3 players); woman initially disagrees with the plan's appeal but ultimately agrees with the man's points.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a new mandatory internship rule: one doubts it builds real leadership skills, and the other argues that many peer schools' similar programs will flood the job market after graduation.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 인턴십 의무화 방침에 대해, 한 학생은 실무 경험이 얕고 졸업 후 취업 경쟁만 심해진다고 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a university requiring students to complete a work placement; the woman opposes it (routine tasks teach nothing new, and graduates will face fierce competition), while the man initially agrees with her points but is persuaded to accept her view.

speakingQ2.g: Two students discuss a letter proposing artwork displays in the student center; the woman objects that heavy foot traffic and natural light make it a poor venue, and the man is persuaded.
speakingQ2.k: 학생회관에 예술 작품을 전시하자는 제안에 대해, 한 학생은 유동 인구와 자연광의 문제로 반대하고 다른 학생은 그 의견에 점차 공감하고 있다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to display art in the student center. The woman opposes it, citing crowds that distract viewers and uncontrolled natural light; the man initially supports the idea but comes around to her view.

speakingQ2.g: A woman argues a dorm renovation will drive students away through noise and higher housing fees, while a man counters that the improved living conditions will eventually draw residents back.
speakingQ2.k: 기숙사 리모델링 계획에 대해 여학생은 공사 소음과 주거비 인상 때문에 학생이 오히려 줄어든다고 반대하고, 남학생은 공사 후 생활 환경 개선으로 장기적 이점이 있다고 본다.
speakingQ2.c: Q2 campus issue: the college's dorm renovation plan; the woman opposes it (construction noise drives students off campus, and raised housing costs deter returning residents), while the man supports it (temporary disruption is outweighed by better long-term living conditions).

speakingQ2.g: A student supports a proposal to widen the campus radio station's programming to a real-world audience, citing career benefits for students and financial gains for the university, based on a peer school's success.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 전용이던 캠퍼스 라디오 방송을 외부 청취자까지 대상으로 넓히자는 제안에 대해, 여학생은 학생 경력과 대학 재정에 도움이 된다며 찬성한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to expand the campus radio station's programming to a wider audience. The woman favors it (student career experience, university funding from commercials); the man only asks questions and agrees, so no clear opposing view appears in this excerpt.

speakingQ2.g: Two students disagree on a university plan to spend two million on a new stadium: one says the money is better spent on academic facilities, the other doubts the stadium will improve town relations.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 새 경기장에 200만 달러를 쓰는 계획을 두고, 학생은 시설 보완이 우선이라 반대하고 학교-지역 관계 개선 효과도 의심한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether the university's new 2-million stadium plan should go ahead. Woman (opposes): money should fix labs, library, and student center first, and a bigger stadium won't win over townspeople since they skip games anyway. Man (supports): the plan addresses the university's weak ties with the town, so it has value.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a proposal to allow snacks in class: one sees it as a fun perk, while the other opposes it because of noise distractions and lost final-review time.
speakingQ2.k: 강의 중 간식 허용 제안을 두고, 한 학생은 찬성 입장에서 즐거움을 강조하지만 다른 학생은 소음으로 인한 방해와 기말 복습 시간 손실을 들어 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to let students eat snacks during class. The woman leans toward approving it as a morale boost, while the man opposes it, citing distraction from chewing and crinkling noises and the loss of valuable exam-review time at the end of the term.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a proposal to change the campus running paths, with the man opposing it on health and relaxation grounds.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 달리기 트랙을 도로처럼 바꾸자는 제안에 대해 두 학생이 반대 의견을 나눈다
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposal to make the running paths look like the surrounding streets (e.g., a paved, hard-surfaced redesign) for safety; the man opposes it because hard surfaces harm joints and runners lose the natural, relaxing escape, while the woman is mostly receptive and asks clarifying questions.

speakingQ2.g: A student doubts that a newspaper letter's proposed fixes for the campus health center, adding space and weekend service, would work, since the center is cramped and most students leave campus on weekends.
speakingQ2.k: 학생이 신문 투고에서 제안한 보건센터 개선안(공간 부족 해결, 주말 운영)에 대해 한 학생은 실효성이 낮다고 비판하고, 다른 학생은 대체로 동의한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the health center's limited space and weekend service. Man: the proposals won't help because the center needs more treatment rooms and weekend demand is low. Woman: largely agrees, noting she also goes home often.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a library plan to install new study units: one wants the money spent on group meeting rooms instead, and both doubt that overcrowding is a real problem.
speakingQ2.k: 도서관 소음 줄이려는 새 칸막이 설치에 대해, 한 학생은 그 예산을 회의실 건설에 쓰자고 하고 다른 학생은 과밀 문제가 없다며 반대한다
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the library's plan to buy new individual study units to cut noise. Man opposes: spend the money on meeting rooms for group work and note empty tables show no overcrowding. Woman agrees with him, saying group work is common and she always finds a whole table free.

speakingQ2.g: The man welcomes the new choir director's plan to join outside competitions and events, expecting more rehearsals and new recruits, while the woman mainly asks clarifying questions and agrees.
speakingQ2.k: 신임 합창단 감독의 외부 대회·행사 참가 계획을 남학생은 반기고, 여학생은 질문하며 대체로 동의함
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the choir director's plan to enter off-campus events and competitions; the man supports it (more practice, attracting new students), while the woman shows no clear opposing view in this excerpt and mostly agrees.

speakingQ2.g: Two students discuss a university plan to charge a yearly fee for a new recreation center to replace the outdated, underused gym.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 낡은 체육 시설을 대신할 새 recreation center를 위해 연간 이용료를 걷는 방안을 두고 두 학생이 찬반을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a yearly fee to fund a new recreation center. Man supports it (old equipment keeps students away, exercise reduces stress, and the cost is small compared with everyday spending); woman first doubts it's worth the money but then agrees the benefits justify it.

speakingQ2.g: Students debate a university's plan to fix old campus buildings: one accepts that action is needed, the other wants less disruptive, cheaper-to-live-with upgrades like new windows and better insulation.
speakingQ2.k: 대학의 건물 개보수 계획이 학업에 지장을 주지 않는 방식이어야 한다는 학생들의 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university's building renovation that would disrupt classroom and study space. Man: accepts that the university must act and largely agrees with the woman's concern about energy efficiency. Woman: opposes a disruptive approach and proposes basic fixes such as replacing drafty windows and insulating the old buildings to keep study spaces available.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate whether the university should replace its weekly newspaper with daily-ish e-mail announcements of campus events.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 두 명이 신문 대신 이메일로 행사 공지를 보내는 새 계획을 두고 찬반을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university plans to send event and activity announcements by e-mail instead of the weekly newspaper. The woman supports it because the weekly paper is too slow and e-mail gives same-day reminders and last-minute cancellation notices, while the man initially doubts students will read e-mail but is persuaded when the woman notes everyone checks e-mail daily and the cafeteria menu could be included.

speakingQ2.g: Both students back the plan to have current students take on admissions work, citing lighter staff workloads and the value of a student's firsthand perspective.
speakingQ2.k: 두 학생 모두 입학처에 학생 인력을 활용하는 방안에 찬성하며, 업무 부담 경감과 학생 시각의 유용성을 근거로 든다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: using current students in admissions tasks; the woman says it is necessary because staff are overloaded, and the man agrees that student perspective would be more helpful, so the excerpt shows no clear opposing view.

speakingQ2.g: Two students discuss the paper's decision to swap out a section, with one arguing that readers already know the major news and that a campus-events listing would be more useful.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 신문이 기존 섹션을 캠퍼스 행사 안내로 바꾸는 결정을 두고, 학생들이 그 효용을 평가하는 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the paper replaces its news-coverage section with a campus-events guide. Woman supports the change (readers already know major stories; campus info is scattered and easy to forget, so a clippable listing helps); man mostly asks for clarification and accepts her reasoning, with no clear opposing view voiced in this excerpt.

speakingQ2.g: Two students disagree about a proposal to shut down a campus dining spot: one values its quiet study atmosphere, while the other says the food has improved under a new manager.
speakingQ2.k: 대학 식당 폐쇄 제안을 두고 한 학생은 조용해서 공부하기 좋다고 찬성하지 않고, 다른 학생은 음식 질이 개선됐다고 반박한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the proposal to close the campus dining hall. Woman opposes it, arguing it is a quiet, productive study spot and the food has improved; man is skeptical, questioning whether the food is good and whether the place is worth keeping, then concedes he will try it.

speakingQ2.g: Two students discuss a proposed graduation ceremony change, and the woman argues that cutting speeches and capping guest invitations would address the stated problems better.
speakingQ2.k: 졸업식 개편안의 두 가지 이유에 대해, 연설 축소와 초청 인원 제한으로 해결할 수 있다는 학생들의 반박
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university's plan to change the graduation ceremony for time and space reasons. The woman opposes the plan and suggests fewer speeches and a lower guest limit; the man largely agrees with her proposed fixes.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate whether replacing advisor meetings with the university website is acceptable: one stresses advisors offer expert guidance beyond posted information, while the other says booking appointments is easy if done early.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들이 대학 웹사이트 대신 지도교수 상담을 받아야 하는지를 두고 한 학생은 상담의 필요성을, 다른 학생은 일정 잡기는 쉽다는 점을 주장한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether the university should replace in-person academic advising with its website; Speaker 1 (man) opposes, arguing advisors provide expert, personalized guidance and that scheduling is manageable; Speaker 2 (woman) largely agrees with the man, so the opposing views are mainly the letter's proposal versus the man's objection, with the woman conceding and noting that scheduling problems are the student's own timing fault.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a proposal to replace textbooks with a campus study device: one doubts its value due to repeated costs and small, hard-to-use controls, while the other sees it as making studying easier.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스에서 교과서 대신 전자기기를 도입하는 방안을 두고, 비용과 사용성 문제를 들어 반대하는 학생과 학습 편의성을 들어 찬성하는 학생의 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: adopting a textbook-replacement device for students; the woman opposes it (costly upgrades, small screen and keypad hard to use, prefers handwritten notes), while the man supports it (easier studying, cheaper than textbooks).

speakingQ2.g: Two music students agree that dorm practice causes noise and that limited practice slots before concerts are a problem, so they welcome the proposal.
speakingQ2.k: 음악 전공 학생들이 기숙사에서 연습하며 겪는 소음 문제와 부족한 연습 시간을 해결할 방안을 두 학생이 지지하는 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a letter proposing more practice space/time slots for music students (the letter's full content is not in the excerpt). Both speakers support it so far: the woman stresses dorm noise and the need for slots before concerts, and the man confirms slots were fully booked. No opposing view appears in this excerpt.

speakingQ2.g: The university plans to clear abandoned bikes; one student agrees but worries it may be unfair to owners, while the other says their poor condition shows they are abandoned and suggests warning notes first.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스에서 방치된 자전거를 치우자는 학교 방침을 두고, 한 학생은 찬성하면서도 공정성을 걱정하고 다른 학생은 자전거 상태를 근거로 방치된 것이 분명하다고 본다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: removing abandoned bikes from campus racks. Man: supports the plan but doubts it is fair, since some bikes may still be in use. Woman: supports it, arguing the damaged, rusty bikes are clearly abandoned and proposing a two-week removal notice.

speakingQ2.g: The woman backs a proposal to address campus parking lot repair problems, citing lost spaces and delays from weather, while the man questions the plan's premise.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 주차장 보수 공사의 문제점에 대해 여학생은 찬성하고, 남학생은 그 근거에 의문을 제기하는 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the proposal to change how parking lot repairs are handled. Woman (for): repairs closed lots, causing parking shortages and late arrivals, and weather prolonged the work. Man (against/skeptical): questions whether those problems are real and whether the proposal's reasons hold.

speakingQ2.g: The man opposes changing the library's movie collection system, arguing the current computer search already works well and student staff cost little, so the budget would not be strained.
speakingQ2.k: 도서관 영화 소장품 관리 방식 변경 제안에 대해, 남학생은 현 시스템이 충분하므로 바꿀 필요가 없고 학생 근로자 인건비도 부담이 없다고 주장한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposal to change how the library handles its movie collection, which the woman supports as easier. Man (opposes): no change is needed because the online catalog already lets users search by title, type, or actor, and student workers are cheap, so the budget is unaffected. Woman (supports): the proposal would make things easier, and she raises concerns about the staff work involved.

speakingQ2.g: Both students support a proposal to run campus buses to the airport during the break, since taxis are costly and fewer students need campus transport then.
speakingQ2.k: 방학 중 캠퍼스 버스를 공항까지 운행하자는 제안에 두 학생이 모두 찬성하며, 택시비 절감과 교내 버스 수요 감소를 이유로 든다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to use campus buses for airport trips during the break; both speakers favor it (the man and woman agree rather than oppose), citing taxi expense and low on-campus bus demand.

speakingQ2.g: Two students disagree about a proposed campus bike policy: one worries shorter rental times would hurt off-campus trips, the other says collecting ID cards would block access to buildings like the library and dining hall.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 자전거 대여 기간 단축과 신분증 보관 제도에 대해 두 학생이 반대 의견을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposed shorter bike loan period and ID-card collateral system. Man opposes both (long weekend trips need full-day bikes; card confiscation blocks library and dining hall access); woman accepts his objections and agrees the card plan would restrict students.

speakingQ2.g: Both speakers support a plan that pairs new students with upperclassmen, since newcomers struggle to learn course and study skills on their own.
speakingQ2.k: 신입생이 수강 정보와 학습 요령을 선배에게서 얻을 수 있게 해주는 계획에 두 화자 모두 찬성한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a plan pairing new students with more experienced students for course and study advice. The man and the woman both support it, so they do not take opposing views.

speakingQ2.g: One student opposes letting people sit in on classes without grades, arguing it would lower discussion quality and add work for the professor, while the other student is more persuaded by the idea.
speakingQ2.k: 성적 없이 청강을 허용하는 제안에 대해, 한 학생은 수업 질과 교수 부담을 이유로 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether non-credit students should be allowed to attend a course (auditing). Man (initially open to it, sees it as the professor's burden being nil) vs. Woman (opposes it: unprepared attendees lower discussion quality and create extra work for the professor).

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a letter proposing laptop use in class: one argues laptops would distract most students and not all can afford them, while the other sees benefits for the professor's teaching.
speakingQ2.k: 강의실에서 노트북 사용을 허용하자는 편지를 두고, 한 학생은 주의 분산 때문에 반대하고 다른 학생은 교수의 수업 활용에 유리하다며 찬성한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposal to allow laptops in classrooms. Man opposes it, saying laptops would distract students and not everyone has one, so they can't serve as a teaching tool; woman supports it, saying she'd use one for notes and the professor could use the internet in teaching.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a proposed campus phone service: one doubts it because the current pay-per-call billing keeps costs low, while the other is unconvinced by the cost concern and ends up favoring keeping the current arrangement.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들이 캠퍼스 공용 전화 도입에 대해 나눈 토론: 여자는 신호 문제 때문에 백업이 필요하다며 찬성하는 반면, 남자는 비용을 우려하고, 여자는 통화당 과금 방식을 근거로 현행 유지를 주장한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university's proposed shared/backup phone service; Speaker W (woman) opposes it, arguing current phone reception is unreliable so a backup is useful but the pay-per-call billing is cheap enough to keep things as they are; Speaker M (man) is concerned about the expense of the new plan, and the two views diverge on whether the added cost is worth the benefit.

speakingQ2.g: A student who is an actor supports a proposal to bring affordable live shows to town, arguing residents lack entertainment and fuller audiences would improve performances.
speakingQ2.k: 마을에 저렴한 공연 기회를 늘리자는 제안에 대해 배우가 찬성하며, 관객이 늘면 공연의 질도 좋아진다고 설명한다.
speakingQ2.c: Q2 issue: a proposal to add local live theater; both speakers appear to support it (the man's reasons: few nearby entertainment options, costly distant professional shows, and fuller houses improving actors' performances; the woman agrees), so no clear opposing views are shown in this excerpt.

speakingQ2.g: The university is considering a carpool program; one student backs it for saving money and cutting pollution, while the other questions whether it would really help the environment.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 학생 카풀 프로그램을 도입하자는 제안에 대해, 여학생은 비용 절감과 환경 개선 효과를 들어 찬성하고 남학생은 환경 효과에 의문을 제기한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university's proposed carpool program for students. Woman (supports): it saves gas money and car maintenance costs and reduces carbon dioxide pollution and improves air quality. Man (opposes/skeptical): doubts that the program would deliver the environmental benefit she claims.

speakingQ2.g: The university plans a new way to help off-campus students connect; one student is hopeful, while the other doubts it will achieve its goal.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 기숙사 밖 학생들을 위해 새로 마련하는 소통 방안의 효과를 두고, 한 학생은 긍정적으로 보고 다른 학생은 실효성에 의문을 제기한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university's plan to connect off-campus students. The man doubts it will work, while the woman supports it, citing dorm lounges as a model and proposing rideshare postings as a useful feature.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a required group project: one worries about being stuck with an unreliable partner and the other argues end-of-term stress makes the project worthless.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들이 기말 그룹 과제를 두고 파트너 의존 불안과 시험 시기 부담 때문에 과제에 부정적인 입장을 나눈다
speakingQ2.c: Q2 campus issue: whether a mandatory end-of-semester group project should be assigned; Woman is opposed (partner risk, exam-period stress, poor quality and frustration), Man is mildly open (sees value in hearing classmates' work and says it is fine).

speakingQ2.s: class size and teaching experience policy
speakingQ2.g: Two students discuss a university decision about class size, questioning the survey behind it and whether teaching experience is valuable.
speakingQ2.k: 대학의 소규모 수업 축소 결정을 두고, 한 학생은 반대하고 다른 학생은 어느 정도 이해하는 입장이다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the university's decision on class size and teacher experience (based on a student survey). Man opposes it, arguing small classes are preferred for participation and that newer teachers are more enthusiastic; woman partly agrees with the decision and notes the survey.

speakingQ2.g: Two students discuss a change to orientation that lets newcomers choose activities and avoid a long mandatory weekend.
speakingQ2.k: 신입생 오리엔테이션을 선택형으로 바꾸는 방안에 대해 학생들이 찬반 의견을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Man: the change is good because it offers choice and frees students from a big weekend time commitment. Woman: she agrees that camping is not for everyone but feels she missed out on a shared experience the old format provided.

speakingQ2.g: Students discuss a proposal to let students sit on a committee that allocates campus group funding; one opposes it, arguing students are too biased and too busy to serve, while the other sees it as a useful experience.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들이 위원회에 참여해 캠퍼스 단체 자금을 결정하는 제안에 대해, 한 학생은 이해관계 때문에 공정하지 않다고 반대하고 다른 학생은 경험에 도움이 된다고 본다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposal for a student committee to decide campus group funding. The man opposes it, saying students are too involved to be fair and too busy to find volunteers; the woman counters that serving would be valuable experience for students.

speakingQ2.g: Two students disagree with a letter writer's claim that the campus café is underused, noting it fills up at night and its lighting has improved.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 두 명이 교내 카페 야간 이용과 조명 개선에 대해 편지 필자의 의견에 반대하는 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether the on-campus café is underused and worth keeping open or improving. Woman disagrees with the letter writer, saying the café is busy in the evenings when students relax and study, and recent renovations fixed the lighting. Man initially doubts the café is busy but is persuaded and agrees the letter writer is wrong.

speakingQ2.s: removing art from campus building wall
speakingQ2.g: A student objects that the new policy will leave a dull, plain building wall and hurt communication, since many students never see the dining hall notices; the other student mostly agrees.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 건물 벽의 예술 작품과 게시물을 없애는 새 정책에 대해 한 학생이 미관 상실과 소통 문제를 들어 반대하고, 다른 학생은 대체로 동의한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a new policy removing the artistic displays from a building wall. Woman opposes it (the building becomes dull and loses character, and dining hall announcements will be missed); man initially questions her but largely concedes, so the opposing views are only partly opposed.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate whether publishing online course evaluations would actually work, one doubting professors would take criticism seriously and the other questioning whether students write useful reviews at all.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 강의 평가를 온라인에 공개하는 방안에 대해 두 학생이 실효성을 놓고 반대 의견을 주고받는다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposal to post online student course evaluations. Woman (skeptic): professors resist public criticism and ignore it, and students rush hurried, vague end-of-term reviews that help no one. Man: future students would benefit from reading them, but he is persuaded by the woman's point that the reviews may be unhelpful.

speakingQ2.g: The man doubts the letter's museum-access idea will ever happen, noting the trip is already easy and cheap for students and that alumni are busy funding other projects.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들의 미술관 방문을 지원하자는 편지 제안은 실현되기 어렵고 불필요하다는 반대 의견이 나온다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a letter proposes a campus-backed museum trip funded partly by alumni. The man opposes it as unnecessary and unfundable, while the woman mostly accepts his facts and shows little resistance.

speakingQ2.s: early textbook and reading list release
speakingQ2.g: Both speakers support the letter's proposal to let students get textbooks and reading assignments before the semester starts, citing cheaper options and time to prepare.
speakingQ2.k: 학생이 학기 전에 교재와 과제 자료를 미리 받을 수 있게 하자는 편지 제안을 두 화자가 모두 지지함
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the letter's proposal for early access to textbooks and reading assignments; the man strongly supports it (saving money on used books, easier preparation before busy term), and the girl agrees, so the excerpt shows no opposing view.

speakingQ2.g: Students debate a university plan to brighten the campus at night: one opposes it as a wasteful expense that would also disrupt astronomy observation, while the other sees the aesthetic appeal.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 야간 조명 확대 계획에 대해, 한 학생은 비용 낭비라며 반대하고 다른 학생은 야경을 근거로 찬성하는 상황이다.
speakingQ2.c: The campus issue is the proposed nighttime lighting plan; the man opposes it as costly and harmful to astronomy observation, while the woman supports it for the attractive night view.

speakingQ2.g: A proposal to clear a wooded area on campus for parking is opposed on the grounds that nearby lots already exist and the remaining trees and shaded study spot should be kept.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 편의를 위해 캠퍼스 숲을 주차장으로 바꾸자는 제안에 대해, 근처에 다른 주차 공간이 있고 남은 녹지를 보존해야 한다는 반대 의견
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a letter proposes clearing a wooded campus area for a parking lot; the woman opposes it (nearby lots exist, walking is fine, trees are scarce and valued), while the man mostly agrees with her points.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate whether the graduation speaker should keep coming from the business sector or be drawn from other professions such as teaching, weighing the publicity benefit for the business school.
speakingQ2.k: 졸업식 연사를 매년 기업인으로 정하는 관행에 대해 교육 분야 인사 등 다양한 직업군으로 바꿔야 한다는 논의
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether the graduation speaker should continue to be a business leader (letter's proposal, which the woman rejects in favor of other professions like teachers) — the man is open to variety but the woman argues the education program needs the publicity, so she sides with a non-business speaker for the education program.

speakingQ2.g: The woman thinks the library's energy-saving plan will backfire, since dim overhead lights will push people to use reading lamps and hot days will drive students to noisier dorms, while the man sees the air-conditioning change as a clear energy saver.
speakingQ2.k: 도서관의 새 에너지 절약 정책이 조명 부족과 냉방 문제로 오히려 학생들의 학습 환경을 악화시킬 수 있다는 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the library's new energy-saving policy (dimmer lights and adjusted air conditioning). The woman (opposing) says it will fail because it wastes savings on individual lamps and drives students away on hot days; the man (partly supportive) says the air-conditioning change will save energy.

speakingQ2.g: A letter proposes making town volunteering compulsory for students; the man argues it would breed resentment, hurt the university's local reputation, and discourage future volunteering, while the woman questions whether students might come to enjoy it.
speakingQ2.k: 학교 측이 학생들에게 지역 봉사를 의무화하자는 편지에 대해, 남학생은 학생들이 억지로 참여해 학교 이미지를 해치고 장기적 봉사 의욕도 생기지 않을 것이라고 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether the university should require students to do local volunteer work. Man opposes, arguing forced volunteering will look bad for the school and reduce future motivation; woman plays devil's advocate, suggesting students might grow to like it.

speakingQ2.g: The female student thinks a mandatory volunteer requirement will breed resentment and that nearby opportunities are impractical without transportation, while the male student mostly agrees.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 학생에게 자원봉사를 의무화하는 방침에 대해, 여학생은 반감을 낳고 교통이 불편해 실효성이 낮다며 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a mandatory volunteer requirement at the Youth Center. The female student opposes it (resentment, poor transport access); the male student is largely supportive at first but agrees with her concerns.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate a proposal for a small campus shop: one backs it for hands-on job experience, the other doubts the need since the cafeteria exists, though the first counters that lines and travel time make a nearby option useful.
speakingQ2.k: 학생 두 명이 캠퍼스 내 소규모 매점 설치 제안에 대해, 한 명은 실무 경험 이점을 들어 찬성하고 다른 한 명은 학생 식당이 있으니 불필요하다고 본다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposed on-campus student-run shop. Male student supports it (valuable work experience, convenience); female student opposes it (cafeteria already available), then the male rebuts that long cafeteria lines and off-campus trips waste time.

speakingQ2.g: The female speaker thinks the study-week idea would encourage cramming and that professors would be too busy to meet students during that period; the male speaker is skeptical and ends up agreeing that professors may lack time.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들이 학기 내내 꾸준히 공부하지 않고 시험 직전에 몰아서 공부하게 만들 수 있고, 시험 준비 기간에는 교수님이 질문에 응대할 시간이 부족하다는 반대 의견
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposed study-week policy. The female speaker opposes it (it encourages cramming and makes professor meetings hard to schedule); the male speaker questions her and tentatively agrees that professors may not have enough time.

speakingQ2.g: Two students doubt a proposal to add a café to the bookstore: one fears books will be damaged by spills, the other notes the Student Center store already sells similar items and the bookstore is too far from classes.
speakingQ2.k: 학내 서점에 카페를 여는 제안에 대해, 한 학생은 책 훼손 위험을 들어 반대하고 다른 학생은 학생회관 편의점과 중복되고 서점이 멀다는 이유로 회의적이다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to add a café inside the bookstore to let students grab food between classes. Female student opposes it, citing risk of ruined books; male student also opposes it, citing the nearby convenience store duplicating the offer and the bookstore's distance from academic buildings.

speakingQ2.g: A male graduate student opposes a new policy that lets undergraduates stay on at the same university, arguing it harms seminar quality and denies students the chance to study elsewhere, while a female student asks him to explain his reasoning.
speakingQ2.k: 새 정책으로 학부생이 같은 대학원에 그대로 진학하게 되면서, 대학원생 입장에서는 세미나 질과 학업 다양성이 떨어질 수 있다고 우려하는 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a policy keeping undergraduates at their own university for graduate study. The male student opposes it, saying large seminars and weaker preparation hurt graduate students and that staying put blocks new schools, professors, and places; the female student mainly asks questions and does not clearly take the opposing side.

speakingQ2.s: dorm kitchen upgrades and cooking classes
speakingQ2.g: Students are discussing a letter proposing new dorm kitchen equipment and peer-led cooking sessions, since the kitchens are currently rarely used.
speakingQ2.k: 기숙사 주방이 거의 쓰이지 않는 문제를 해결하기 위해 주방 설비를 새로 갖추고 학생 간 요리 교실을 열자는 제안에 대한 대화
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to upgrade dorm kitchens and start peer cooking lessons; both speakers support the letter, with the male student recounting a bad kitchen experience and the female student agreeing that more students would then use the kitchens.

speakingQ2.s: math building café and charging stations
speakingQ2.g: Two students both support a proposal to add a food spot and laptop charging stations in the math building, since food is far away and the building lacks outlets.
speakingQ2.k: 수학관에 간식 공간과 노트북 충전 시설을 만들자는 제안에 두 학생이 모두 찬성한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposed café and laptop-charging area in the math building; the two speakers do not oppose each other, both favor it for convenience and for the lack of charging spots.

speakingQ2.g: Jason's letter proposes turning the unused campus field into a parking lot; the female student opposes this because students use the open space and existing parking is sufficient, while the male student mostly agrees but notes commuters may need spaces.
speakingQ2.k: 캠퍼스 빈터를 주차장으로 바꾸자는 제안에 대해, 한 학생은 휴식과 공부에 쓰이므로 유지해야 한다고 반대하고 다른 학생은 기숙사 주차 공간이 충분하다는 점을 들어 그 주장에 동의한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: whether to convert Sander's Field, an open area no longer used for sports, into a parking lot. Female student opposes (students use it to relax and study, and dorm parking already suffices); male student is mostly sympathetic to her view but raises the commuter-parking concern, which she counters by saying commuters prefer lots near classrooms.

speakingQ2.g: Two students debate whether a new online tool showing degree requirements is necessary, weighing its benefits for students who miss required courses and for busy advisors.
speakingQ2.k: 학생들은 학위 이수 요건을 온라인에서 확인할 수 있는 새 도구가 필요한지, 그리고 그것이 학생과 지도교수에게 도움이 되는지를 논의한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: a proposed online tool listing degree requirements. The male student supports it, arguing it prevents missed required courses and frees advisors for serious advising; the female student initially doubts it is needed, then partly concedes it could help after citing a friend's delayed graduation.

speakingQ2.g: The university plans to move the cafeteria into the library basement; both students think it is a bad idea because it would encourage unhealthy snacking and distract people from studying.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 학생식당을 도서관 지하로 옮기려는 계획에 대해, 두 학생 모두 건강에 나쁜 간식 위주 식단과 집중력 저하 우려를 들어 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: relocating the cafeteria to the library basement. Speaker 1 opposes it, citing unhealthy library snacks and temptation to socialize; Speaker 2 first questions this, then agrees and adds that the plan may backfire.

speakingQ2.g: The university plans to pair roommates by shared interests; the male student supports it, while the female student argues that differing interests don't prevent friendship and that move-out rates won't drop much.
speakingQ2.k: 대학이 룸메이트를 공통 관심사 기준으로 배정하는 방안을 두고, 남학생은 찬성하고 여학생은 관심사가 달라도 잘 지낼 수 있으며 이사율도 크게 줄지 않을 것이라며 반대한다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: pairing roommates by shared interests. Male student: supports it as sensible. Female student: opposes it, arguing friendship doesn't require similar interests and people will still move out for other reasons such as schedules or location.

speakingQ2.s: lawn damage and campus recreation space
speakingQ2.g: Two students doubt that banning the students who damage the lawn would fix a problem caused by heavy foot traffic, and they debate whether a nearby alternative play space would be practical.
speakingQ2.k: 잔디밭 훼손 문제에 대한 편지 제안(학생 퇴출, 대체 놀이 공간)의 효과를 두고 두 학생이 의견을 나눈다.
speakingQ2.c: Campus issue: the letter's proposals to restrict lawn users and provide a play area. The female student argues they would not solve the problem because everyone crosses the lawn and the gym is too far; the male student concedes the substitute might help a little but agrees the distance makes it impractical.

speakingQ3.g: Senior managers' disapproval led colleagues to abandon a sound proposal to avoid risk, and the company later lost customers to a competitor.
speakingQ3.k: 회의에서 상급자의 반대로 팀원들이 의견을 바꾸고, 결국 잘못된 결정으로 회사가 손해를 본 사례
speakingQ3.c: Q3: Concept is groupthink, where people conform to the group or leaders' views despite private doubts; the professor illustrates it with his own experience at a computer company, where his design-update proposal was dropped after senior managers objected and a competitor then gained customers.

speakingQ3.g: When people know they are being watched, they perform tasks faster, but common errors also rise, as shown by shoe-tying and typing examples.
speakingQ3.k: 누군가 지켜볼 때 사람은 활동 속도가 빨라지지만 평소 실수도 함께 늘어난다는 것을 보여준다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: audience effect (being observed speeds up performance); professor's example: students tying shoes faster when watched, and typing faster but with more mistakes.

speakingQ3.g: The professor describes how, facing a clash between gaming and schoolwork, he resolved the conflict by redefining academic success as doing well only in courses tied to his intended career.
speakingQ3.k: 교수는 학업과 게임 사이의 갈등을 해결하기 위해 '성공의 정의'를 진로와 직접 관련된 과목으로 좁혀 재해석했던 자신의 경험을 설명한다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: reinterpreting a situation to reduce internal conflict; Professor's example: he dismissed his failing chemistry grade because it was irrelevant to his goal of becoming a sociologist.

speakingQ3.g: People often reveal emotions through unconscious facial and bodily signals, even when they try to hide them.
speakingQ3.k: 사람은 기쁨이나 고통을 의식하지 못한 채 얼굴과 몸짓으로 드러내며, 감정을 숨기려 해도 완벽하게 가려지지 않는다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: emotions leak out through involuntary nonverbal cues despite conscious effort to conceal them; professor's example: his delighted reaction to an uncle's surprise visit versus his hidden pain after hitting his thumb, which his daughter still noticed through his trembling voice and posture.

speakingQ3.g: Companies make different TV ads for the same product depending on the audience of each program.
speakingQ3.k: 같은 제품이라도 시청하는 프로그램의 시청자층에 따라 서로 다른 광고를 만들어 공략한다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: tailoring ads to the viewers of specific shows; example: one cell phone marketed as fun to teens during pop/teen shows and as efficient to business people during business news.

speakingQ3.g: Implicit memory shapes behavior without conscious recall, illustrated by a highway billboard that drivers forget seeing but that later influences the animal names they produce.
speakingQ3.k: 의식하지 못하는 암묵 기억은 광고 같은 자극의 영향을 받으며, 그 예로 고속도로 광고판이 기억하지 못하는 사이에 운전자의 단어 떠올리기에 영향을 준 실험을 들 수 있다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: implicit memory, which operates without conscious awareness; Example: drivers who cannot recall a billboard for the car Panther still name Panther when asked for an animal starting with P.

speakingQ3.g: Children learn appropriate classroom behavior because misbehavior brings punishment while good behavior brings rewards that reinforce it.
speakingQ3.k: 아이들은 나쁜 행동에 대한 처벌과 좋은 행동에 대한 칭찬을 겪으며 교실에서 올바른 행동을 익힌다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: operant conditioning, where consequences shape future behavior; Professor's example: a new schoolchild who misbehaves is punished and then praised for quiet, attentive conduct, so they keep behaving well.

speakingQ3.g: Animals can escape predators by suddenly revealing bright colors that startle attackers, or by producing flashes of reflected light that make them hard to track.
speakingQ3.k: 동물이 포식자를 피하는 방법으로, 갑자기 드러나는 밝은 색이나 번쩍이는 빛으로 놀라게 하거나 추적을 방해하는 두 가지 사례를 설명한다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: flash coloration and flashing light as predator defense; professor's examples: the Peanut Bug's hidden back wings that suddenly open to startle predators, and the morpho butterfly's shiny wings whose flashes of reflected light confuse birds.

speakingQ3.g: An opening establishing shot of a gloomy 1940s city tells viewers the setting, era, and mood before any action begins.
speakingQ3.k: 영화 첫 장면의 도시 이미지가 시대, 배경, 분위기를 미리 알려 주어 이후 장면을 예측하게 해 준다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: an establishing shot sets up a scene's time, place, and tone. Example: the speaker's movie opening, a dark, foggy 1940s city skyline, let him predict a mysterious detective story before the characters appeared.

speakingQ3.g: Shows and matching toys reinforce each other: children who watch a program want its toys, and the toys in turn drive more viewing.
speakingQ3.k: TV 프로그램과 연계된 장난감이 아이들 사이에서 인기를 끄는 현상을 개인 사례로 설명
speakingQ3.c: Concept: cross-promotion between a TV show and toys; the professor's example is his childhood Action Hero craze and his daughter's Rosa doll, whose TV show quickly became as popular as the doll.

speakingQ3.g: Outsider artists create distinctive work independently, often inventing their own solutions to technical problems, as shown by a Chicago painter who pasted newspaper figures into his large landscapes.
speakingQ3.k: 정식 교육 없이 사적으로 작업한 외부 예술가가 독창적인 방식으로 만든 작품 사례
speakingQ3.c: Concept: outsider art is original work made without formal training or public audience; example: Henry Dodger's long painting where he cut out newspaper pictures of children and pasted them into his painted scenery to solve his difficulty drawing people.

speakingQ3.g: Brief, barely perceptible images can unconsciously shape later judgments about a person's character.
speakingQ3.k: 아주 짧게 노출된 이미지가 이후 사람에 대한 판단을 무의식적으로 바꾼다는 실험 사례
speakingQ3.c: Concept: subliminal priming, where a fleeting stimulus influences later perception without awareness. Professor's example: viewers flashed an angry or happy boy with cake, then judged a neutral image of the same boy, rating him negatively or positively accordingly.

speakingQ3.g: Objects seem to change in shape or size with viewing angle or distance, yet we still perceive them as unchanged.
speakingQ3.k: 물체가 시점에 따라 모양이나 크기가 달라 보여도 사람은 같은 물체로 인식한다
speakingQ3.c: concept: perceptual constancy (perceiving objects as stable despite changing sensory input); professor's example: a round plate viewed at an angle looks oval but is still seen as the same plate, and a professor who appears smaller from the back row is still recognized as the same size and person

speakingQ3.s: career decisions and resistance to change
speakingQ3.g: People often stay with a familiar job rather than take a better opportunity because a change feels too risky.
speakingQ3.k: 익숙해진 현재 직업을 지키려고 원하던 더 나은 기회를 거절하는 심리를 설명한다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: people resist a change that would improve their situation once they become comfortable where they are. Professor's example: a friend who turned down his dream film-reviewer job, with higher pay, because he had grown used to his news-reporter role.

speakingQ3.g: A researcher who falsely believed one monkey group was smarter gave them more encouragement, so that group was trained faster even though the groups were actually equal.
speakingQ3.k: 연구자가 원숭이의 지능을 잘못 알고 있었을 때, 똑똑하다고 믿은 집단을 더 격려해 실제로 훈련이 더 빨리 끝났다는 실험 사례
speakingQ3.c: Q3: concept of expectancy (self-fulfilling prophecy) – the researcher's belief about the monkeys' intelligence shaped his behavior, and the professor's example is the monkey training experiment in which the supposedly smart group was trained about two hours faster.

speakingQ3.g: When individual contributions cannot be identified, people in a group work less hard than those working alone, as shown by a potato-peeling experiment.
speakingQ3.k: 집단으로 일할 때 개인의 기여가 드러나지 않으면 사람들이 노력을 줄인다는 실험 결과
speakingQ3.c: Q3 concept: social loafing (reduced effort in groups when individual output is hidden); professor's example: a potato-peeling study comparing solo workers with group workers whose individual totals were unrecorded

speakingQ3.g: A dog's baring of teeth began as a step before biting but evolved into a warning signal that deters threats without an actual attack.
speakingQ3.k: 개가 위협을 느낄 때 이빨을 드러내는 행동은 원래 물기 직전의 준비 동작이었으나, 반복 경험을 통해 실제 공격 없이 경고 신호로 기능하게 된 방어 수단으로 발전했다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: a behavior can evolve from a physical precursor into a communicative signal; professor's example: a dog showing its teeth to ward off threats without biting.

speakingQ3.g: Pronghorns evolved great speed to escape lions that once roamed North American plains, even though those lions have since vanished and today's predators are slower.
speakingQ3.k: 프롱혼은 빠른 속도가 원래 사자 같은 포식자를 피하기 위해 진화했지만, 사자가 사라진 뒤에도 그 속도가 남아 있다는 내용이다.

speakingQ3.g: Children learn which behaviors to copy by watching whether a sibling's actions get rewarded or punished.
speakingQ3.k: 아이는 형제가 보상받거나 벌받는 행동을 지켜보면서 그 행동을 따라 하거나 피하도록 배운다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: children imitate behaviors they observe being reinforced and avoid those they see punished. Professor's example: a younger brother watches his sister win a toy through tantrums, so he is likely to throw tantrums too; if the sister is punished instead, he is unlikely to do the same.

speakingQ3.g: Buying into an established chain's name and operating system lowers a startup's risk because demand and proven methods already exist, though the owner gives up much of the freedom to run things independently.
speakingQ3.k: 프랜차이즈 가맹을 통해 기존 브랜드의 이름과 운영 방식을 빌리면 신규 사업의 성공 가능성이 높아지지만, 그만큼 독자적인 운영 자율성은 줄어든다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: franchising, where a new owner pays for a known brand and must follow its training and standards. Professor's example: opening a pizza restaurant under the Pizza Town name, which brings guaranteed customer recognition and a tested method in exchange for limited control.

speakingQ3.g: A teacher whose young pupil kept shouting answers instead of raising a hand stopped the behavior by explaining that it was unfair to classmates, and the student then complied.
speakingQ3.k: 교사가 아이들에게 손을 들고 발언하도록 한 규칙을 어기는 학생에게 공정성 문제를 짚어 주자 행동이 바뀌었다는 사례
speakingQ3.c: Professor's example: a teacher explains to a child that calling out without raising a hand is unfair to classmates, and the child then consistently raises her hand, illustrating how a brief explanation of fairness can correct a rule-breaking behavior.

speakingQ3.s: escalation of commitment and sunk costs
speakingQ3.g: The professor describes how he kept investing in a renovation despite mounting problems and his wife's warnings, illustrating how past investment can drive people to persist in a bad decision.
speakingQ3.k: 교수는 자신이 낡은 집을 수리하며 점점 더 많은 돈을 쏟아붓고도 손을 떼지 못했던 경험으로, 이미 투입한 비용 때문에 잘못된 결정을 고수하는 심리를 설명한다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: escalation of commitment, where prior investment pushes people to keep spending on a failing course. Professor's example: buying and repairing an old country house, where each new problem made him more determined to continue rather than cut losses.

speakingQ3.g: People tend to adjust their clothing to match the norms of whichever social group they belong to, as the professor's own shift from casual to dressier clothes shows.
speakingQ3.k: 사람들은 자신이 속한 집단의 규범에 맞춰 옷차림을 바꾸는 경향이 있으며, 교수는 자신의 대학 시절과 직장 경험을 예로 든다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: group norms shape what people wear, so individuals conform to their surroundings; Example: the professor's casual style changed to a dressier one after moving from art-student friends to professional coworkers.

speakingQ3.g: Local residents saved a threatened parrot whose rainforest habitat was being cleared by distributing educational brochures and securing protected land, which let the bird and dependent species recover.
speakingQ3.k: 남미 우림에서 나무 벌채로 위기에 처한 마코앵무를 지키기 위해 주민들이 홍보 책자와 보호구역 조성으로 개체 수를 회복시킨 사례
speakingQ3.c: concept-example: the professor illustrates how a single endangered species' decline reflects habitat loss, and how awareness plus protected land can reverse it

speakingQ3.s: adoption of telephone for personal use
speakingQ3.g: The telephone was first adopted only by businesses; the public resisted personal calls over concerns about unseen voices and etiquette, but after roughly three decades, shared norms made personal calling widely accepted.
speakingQ3.k: 전화는 처음에 기업만 쓰다가, 사람들이 보이지 않는 대화와 예절 문제로 꺼렸지만 약 30년에 걸쳐 가정에 보급되고 개인 통화가 자연스러운 관습이 되었다.
speakingQ3.c: Professor's concept: social acceptance of a new technology shifts gradually as people get used to it and establish etiquette norms; example: the telephone's move from business tool to personal device over about 30 years.

speakingQ3.g: Rainforest epiphytes use leaf structure to funnel and store rainwater, then harvest nutrients from decomposing debris in that reservoir.
speakingQ3.k: 열대우림 나무 위에 붙어 사는 식물이 잎 모양으로 빗물을 모아 저장하고, 그 안에서 분해된 잔해로 영양분을 얻는 방식
speakingQ3.c: Concept: some canopy plants that grow on trees adapt by collecting water and nutrients in specialized leaves; Professor's example: a funnel-leaved epiphyte that stores rainwater and gets nitrogen-rich fertilizer from decaying matter.

speakingQ3.g: Individual ants cannot cross a gap alone, so they link their bodies one after another to form a living bridge that the group uses to reach food.
speakingQ3.k: 개미들은 먹이로 가는 길에 생긴 틈을 자기 몸으로 다리를 만들어 건넌다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: collective self-assembly of ants into a bridge; Example: ants crossing a gap between tree branches to reach food.

speakingQ3.g: A company's ad openly admits its cookware costs more, then argues the higher price pays off over time through a lifetime warranty.
speakingQ3.k: 비싼 가격을 먼저 솔직히 인정하고 장기적 절약 효과를 내세우는 광고 전략의 예시
speakingQ3.c: Concept: openly acknowledging a high price and reframing it as long-term savings; Example: a TV ad for premium pots and pans that admits the cost and highlights a lifetime free-replacement warranty.

speakingQ3.g: A northeastern American squirrel gathers and prepares nuts in autumn, then scatters single nuts across many buried spots so that losing some still leaves enough food for winter.
speakingQ3.k: 북미 북동부 다람쥐는 가을에 견과류를 찾아 손질한 뒤 여러 곳에 하나씩 묻어 두어, 겨울 식량을 확보하고 일부를 잃어도 생존하도록 한다.
speakingQ3.c: concept-example: the professor illustrates food caching behavior with the squirrel, explaining why it buries each nut in a separate hole

speakingQ3.g: Anger about a trivial disagreement can actually stem from a different underlying worry, and recognizing that hidden source can repair the relationship.
speakingQ3.k: 겉으로 드러난 다툼의 원인과 실제 감정의 뿌리가 다를 수 있으며, 이를 깨닫는 것이 관계 회복에 도움이 된다는 내용
speakingQ3.c: Concept: emotional displacement, where a person's upset is aimed at the wrong trigger; Professor's example: the daughter argued with her friend over a movie choice but was really anxious about her new camp counselor job, and once she named that anxiety and apologized, the friendship was restored.

speakingQ3.g: People mentally sort money by where it came from, so earnings from a side job get spent more freely than a regular paycheck, even when the total is the same.
speakingQ3.k: 사람들은 돈의 출처에 따라 마음속으로 다른 용도를 정해, 같은 액수라도 쓰는 방식이 달라진다는 개념
speakingQ3.c: Concept: mental accounting, where people treat money from different sources as separate; Professor's example: a waiter who saved his salary for a house but spent his tips on dinners and entertainment, which delayed his goal.

speakingQ3.g: After a purchase, people gradually stop noticing the drawbacks they once worried about and focus on the benefits, as shown by a friend who forgot a house's small size.
speakingQ3.k: 사람들은 구매 후 시간이 지나면 처음에 신경 쓰던 단점을 점차 잊고 장점만 기억하게 된다는 내용이다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: people's attention to a purchase's downsides fades over time; Example: the professor's friend who bought a house, first worried about its small size, but later could not recall that concern and praised only its location.

speakingQ3.g: A moth population shrinks when a dry year cuts its food supply, then rebounds to its earlier size once rainfall and plant growth return.
speakingQ3.k: 가뭄으로 먹이가 줄었다가 강우 회복 후 개체수가 원래 수준으로 돌아오는 나방 사례
speakingQ3.c: Concept: density-dependent population change driven by food availability; Professor's example: a European red-and-black moth feeding on Ragwort, whose numbers fall in a drought year and recover after rains return.

speakingQ3.g: Experiment showing that people tend to prefer stimuli they saw briefly before, even when they don't consciously recall seeing them.
speakingQ3.k: 짧게 노출된 도형을 나중에 기억하지 못해도 더 선호하게 되는 현상을 보여준 실험
speakingQ3.c: Concept: repeated or prior exposure to a stimulus increases preference for it, even without awareness; Professor's example: students shown unusual shapes for a split second in dim light later preferred those shapes over new ones when paired.

speakingQ3.g: Farmers can use chickens in a mobile, floorless coop to clear weeds and enrich soil before planting, which benefits both the chickens and the crop.
speakingQ3.k: 닭을 이용해 밭의 잡초를 제거하고 토양을 개선하는 방법을 바퀴 달린 바닥 없는 닭장 사례로 설명함
speakingQ3.c: Concept: using chickens to prepare a field before planting; Professor's example: a wheeled, floorless coop moved across a bean field so chickens eat weeds and improve soil before the beans grow.

speakingQ3.g: Audiences gradually shift from noticing a performer's disguise to emotionally connecting with the character he portrays.
speakingQ3.k: 관객은 배우의 변신을 통해 처음에는 거리를 두다가 점차 등장인물에게 감정적으로 몰입하게 된다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: audiences empathize with a character through an actor's transformation; example: the professor's college roommate playing an old father, which moved the professor from distraction to worry and relief.

speakingQ3.g: Forager ants adjust what food they collect depending on whether the colony has mainly adults needing energy or newborns needing protein.
speakingQ3.k: 개미 탐색 일개미가 colony의 구성원 변화에 따라 당분이 많은 먹이와 단백질이 많은 먹이를 번갈아 가져온다.
speakingQ3.c: Q3/Q4: the concept is that foragers adapt their food choices to the colony's changing needs; the professor's example is ants bringing sugary fruit when adults dominate and protein-rich leaves or mushrooms when larvae are born.

speakingQ3.g: Mites rely on hummingbirds to ferry them between short-lived tropical flowers, since the birds are unharmed by the hitchhiking mites.
speakingQ3.k: 진드기는 빨리 시드는 열대 꽃 사이를 이동하기 위해 벌새에 붙어 옮겨 다니며, 벌새는 해를 입지 않는다.
speakingQ3.c: Q3 concept: mutualistic-style dispersal where mites hitch rides on hummingbirds; professor's example is mites catching rides on hummingbirds to reach new flowers for nectar and pollen.

speakingQ3.g: An independent expert's certification reassures buyers because the expert gains nothing from the sale, and a jewelry shop's use of an expert's certification illustrates this.
speakingQ3.k: 판매자와 이해관계가 없는 독립 전문가의 인증이 소비자 신뢰를 높인다는 개념을 보석상 사례로 설명함
speakingQ3.c: Concept: a disinterested third-party expert's certification builds buyer trust; Example: a jewelry store displays a certified expert's authentication to justify high prices.

speakingQ3.g: Two rattlesnakes competing for the same burrow settle their dispute through pushing contests and never bite each other, even when one has a clear chance to.
speakingQ3.k: 두 방울뱀이 같은 먹이굴을 두고 싸울 때 상대를 물지 않고 힘겨루기로 승부를 가린다는 관찰 내용
speakingQ3.c: Q3/Q4: concept = ritualized combat that avoids injury; professor's example = two rattlesnakes wrestling over one hole, with the winner sparing the loser

speakingQ3.g: An early impression formed in a person's first days can stick, leading observers to notice only the behavior that fits their original judgment.
speakingQ3.k: 초기의 한 번의 인상이 이후의 평가를 고정시키며, 사람들은 그 판단에 맞는 행동만 골라 보게 된다.
speakingQ3.c: Concept: early first impressions shape later evaluations, with people selectively attending to confirming evidence; Example: the professor got a lasting positive label from one early success, while a coworker's single early mistake led the boss to see her as unreliable, ignoring her later competence.

speakingQ3.g: Prairie dogs initially treat humans as predators and sound alarms, but after repeated harmless encounters they gradually stop reacting.
speakingQ3.k: 프레리도그는 처음엔 사람을 위협으로 보고 경고 반응을 하지만, 사람이 해를 끼치지 않고 반복해서 지나가면 점차 그 반응을 멈춘다.
